answer: Let reputation decay unless an agent keeps doing useful, attested work, and never let a brand-new identity inherit the standing of an old one. A sybil operator must therefore maintain every fake continuously, which is far costlier than creating it. The karst history shows how long an identity has actually worked, the velvet decay removes idle or flagged accounts from queues, and the comet renewal requires fresh peer attestation, so abandoned clones quietly lose access instead of accumulating influence. The defence works because it prices identity, not because it bans newcomers.
